depiction_rules.notes: Shared Varaha identity contract for the D012/D013 candidate sets, still draft and not a user-approved character sheet. Preserve the boar identity, earth-pigment palette, matte contour, and beneficent divine presence across chapters. D012's source scenes are non-combat growth, search, and Earth-lifting scenes; apply its natural-boar anatomy and no-weapon constraints only to those D012 scenes. D013's canonical Hiraṇyākṣa duel explicitly names a mace (13-4), discus (13-5/13-6), and toe-stomp (13-7). Those exact source-grounded actions may require scene-specific pose, limb arrangement, or attributes. Do not invent an additional form: D013's plan owns its scene-specific count and action decisions.

visual_bible.shared_core_identity: One divine Varaha identity across chapters: unmistakable boar head, elongated snout, tusks, upright ears, beneficent divine presence, firm matte contour, and the series' earth-pigment palette. Keep the same identity without forcing one pose or limb arrangement across every source scene.
visual_bible.form: Keep the same recognizable divine boar identity while following the exact scene source. D012 depicts infant, growing, roaring, descending, searching, and Earth-lifting boar scenes; use coherent natural-boar anatomy there. D013's duel may use only the scene-specific pose and attributes justified by its canonical action and recorded in the D013 plan. Do not infer a new form from familiarity or composite intake iconography.
visual_bible.growth: The same recognizable boar identity changes scale from thumb-sized to elephant-sized and mountain-sized; avoid duplicate unrelated boars except when explicitly showing the growth transition as one continuous scale progression.
visual_bible.expression: Vigorous and awe-inspiring; fierce roar and focused search below water, while remaining divine and beneficent. In S007, incline the face toward the sages in a blessing glance.
visual_bible.anatomy: For D012 non-combat scenes only: one boar head, one coherent torso, two natural forelegs and two hind legs; no added human arms or weapons. A single tusk supports Earth in S009-S010. This D012 constraint does not set D013's limb count or pose; the D013 plan records only what its verified scene action requires.
visual_bible.ornament: Keep divine markings and restrained painted-ochre ornament subordinate to the boar anatomy. For D012 non-combat scenes, do not infer extra limbs, weapons, or battle posture from composite reference art. D013 may depict only source-grounded duel attributes and actions specified in its plan.
visual_bible.palette: Traditional matte earth ochre, warm cream and deep brown contours; local boar fur may use muted reddish-brown, dark brown, or natural boar tones without glossy rendering.

never: For D012 non-combat scenes only: no extra heads, tusks, legs, arms, or detached body parts beyond coherent natural-boar anatomy
For D012 infant-boar scenes only: no human baby face on the infant boar
For D012 non-combat scenes only: no aggressive demon or warrior characterization
For D012 non-combat scenes only: no unrelated weapons or four-armed humanoid body; this restriction does not prohibit D013's source-grounded mace, discus, or toe-stomp actions
Across chapters: no photorealism, glossy skin, reflective gold, cinematic lighting, text, logo, or watermark
cross_chapter_boundary: D012 verses 12-1 to 12-10 describe infant, growing, roaring, descending, searching, and lifting forms of a boar without prescribing combat weapons or extra limbs; natural-boar anatomy/no-weapons constraints apply to D012 non-combat scenes only. Stotra Nidhi's D013 verses 13-4 to 13-7 explicitly describe the mace duel, discus use, and toe-stomp. Preserve the shared identity and palette; D013's plan owns any scene-specific pose, limb count, and action, with no invented form.
